age.evidence: Age of rats is not stated in the manuscript.

sex.evidence: Long Evans rats (n = 78, M, Janvier Labs) used in experiment 1... Rats in experiment 2 (Long Evans, n = 18, M, Janvier Labs)... It should be noted that only male rats were used in this study.

dosing.doses_raw: Occupancy: 0.05, 0.20, 1.00 mg/kg s.c.; WBS dose-response: 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 1.0, 3.0, 6.0 mg/kg s.c.; repeated regimen: 0.05 mg/kg s.c. every second day for 21 days.
dosing.evidence: The treatment group received 0.05 mg/kg psilocybin s.c. every second day for 21 days... psilocybin (vehicle, 0.05 mg/kg, 0.20 mg/kg and 1.00 mg/kg in saline, s.c.)... saline or psilocybin at a range of doses (0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 1.0, 3.0, 6.0 mg/kg in saline, s.c.).

handling.evidence: Rats were habituated to the environment for 12 days after arrival, but no explicit handling protocol is described.

group_housing.evidence: Long Evans rats (n = 78, M, Janvier Labs) used in experiment 1 were housed in pairs... Rats in experiment 2 were housed four to a cage.

day_night_flipped.evidence: All animals were kept at a 12-h light/dark (light 6-18) cycle. All experiments were carried out during the light phase beginning at ~10:00 h.

assays.assay_description: Acute psilocybin (0.05-6 mg/kg s.c.) administered, then rats placed in a 20x20 cm arena with 30 cm walls for 1 h; wet back shakes (rat equivalent of head-twitch response) manually scored from video.

application_type.evidence: saline or psilocybin at a range of doses (0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 1.0, 3.0, 6.0 mg/kg in saline, s.c.)

setup_habituation.evidence: No habituation to the WBS arena is described.

setup_restrain.evidence: placed in a 20 × 20 cm arena with 30 cm high walls including one clear Plexiglas wall to allow for video recording

food_restriction.evidence: No food in the arena during the 1-h recording.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in the arena during the 1-h recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: They were then placed in a 20 × 20 cm arena... for one hour.

sample_size.evidence: Long Evans rats (n = 22) were given saline or psilocybin at a range of doses.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin induced a classic inverted U-shaped wet-back-shake response. Low doses (≤0.25 mg/kg) did not differ from saline, 1 mg/kg evoked a significant increase (~8.5 shakes/10 min), and shakes declined again at higher sedative doses.
outcomes.statistics: One-way ANOVA F(6,17)=2.89, P=0.04; 1 mg/kg vs control P=0.01.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin at low doses did not induce any significant change in wet-back shakes, whereas 1 mg/kg evoked a significant increase (P = 0.01, 8.5 ± 5.8 per 10 min) compared to the control group.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Only wet back shakes were scored.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Total counts reported, no within-session time-course analysis.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No sequence or transition analysis reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Wet back shake is the rat equivalent of head-twitch response (explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours).

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Wet back shakes were manually scored.

E3_bedding.evidence: The arena was cleaned and disinfected between trials, indicating a bare floor.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in arena.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline recorded in same assay.

assays.assay_description: Open field in 80.5x80.5 cm square arena (40.5 cm walls). Experiment 1: 40 min in a familiar arena (animals pre-habituated). Experiment 2: 15 min in a novel arena (naive). Distance, center entries/time, supported/unsupported rearing, and grooming frequency/duration were measured.

application_type.evidence: 0.05 mg/kg psilocybin s.c. every second day for 21 days

setup_habituation.evidence: Animals in the first experiment were habituated to the open-field in the days prior to the test (Exp 1); Exp 2 animals were naïve.

setup_restrain.evidence: rats were placed in the center of an 80.5 × 80.5 cm square field; freely moving.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in the OFT arena during recording; experiment 1 rats were on a restrictive diet (6 pellets/day) for startle testing motivation.

water_restriction.evidence: No water provided in the OFT arena during testing.

time_to_assay.evidence: behavioral tests were done on the day following the last treatment

sample_size.evidence: Experiment 1: 2 cohorts of n = 18 (36 rats); Experiment 2: n = 18.

outcomes.summary: Repeated low-dose psilocybin did not alter locomotion, center entries/time, or rearing in either familiar (Exp 1) or novel (Exp 2) open fields. Self-grooming frequency was reduced by ~14% in the familiar OFT (P=0.016).
outcomes.statistics: Self-grooming frequency: unpaired two-tailed t-test, P = 0.016. Other measures: no significant effects.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin microdosing reduced the overall self-grooming frequency by 14% in the microdosing compared to control animals (unpaired, two-tailed t-test, P = 0.016).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Distance traveled, center entries, time in center, unsupported rearing, supported rearing, grooming frequency, grooming duration.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Self-grooming increase over time and peak at 15-35 min in both psilocybin-treated and control animals (within-session time-course).

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: Grooming microstructure not analyzed: 'While we did not analyze the microstructure of their grooming sequences in detail'.

B4_ethological.evidence: Grooming and rearing scored as distinct ethological acts.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Tracking via Ethovision XT 11.5 (position tracking, excluded from B7); rearing and grooming scored manually.

E1_environment_type.evidence: 80.5 × 80.5 cm square field with 40.5 cm walls.

E3_bedding.evidence: Standard open-field floor with no bedding mentioned.

E6_spatial.evidence: Single open square arena with virtual center/border zones.

E7_social_context.evidence: Single animal in the arena during testing.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in arena during recording.

D1_continuity.evidence: Each animal recorded in a single OFT session.

D2_session_duration.evidence: baseline recording of open field behavior for 40 min (Exp 1); 15 min in Exp 2.

D3_recording_days.evidence: OFT test performed on a single day per animal.

D4_baseline.evidence: Habituation occurred without data collection used as baseline.

D5_followup.evidence: Test conducted on the day following the last treatment (~24 h post-dose).

assays.assay_description: 80-min session in the StartFear Combined startle chamber: 10-min acclimation, basal startle (70-120 dB pulses on a prior day), then PPI session with 5-min exploration, short-term habituation block (10 pulses, 110 dB), PPI block (7 trial types with 65-81 dB pre-pulses preceding 110 dB pulses, 15 trials each), and a second STH block. Startle amplitude, latency, %PPI and habituation were measured.

application_type.evidence: 0.05 mg/kg psilocybin s.c. every second day for 21 days

setup_habituation.evidence: After an exploration period of ten min with a constant background white noise of 65 dB for acclimation... Block I was a five min exploration period.

setup_restrain.evidence: Startle tests were conducted in the StartFear Combined system (Panlab Harvard Apparatus), which uses a restrainer/holder for the rat during recording.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in startle chamber during recording; Exp 1 rats were on a 6 pellets/day diet.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in startle chamber during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: behavioral tests were done on the day following the last treatment

sample_size.evidence: Experiment 1: 2 cohorts of n = 18 male rats.

outcomes.summary: Repeated low-dose psilocybin did not alter basal startle amplitude, latency, or %PPI at any pre-pulse intensity. Control rats showed expected short-term habituation (P=0.007), whereas psilocybin-treated rats showed more variable, blunted habituation.
outcomes.statistics: Short-term habituation in controls: P = 0.007; no group differences in SR, latency, or %PPI.
outcomes.evidence: There were no group differences in SR to pulse (P) and pre-pulse + pulse (PP + P)... There was no group difference in latency from the startle pulse to maximum peak of startle or in %PPI.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Startle amplitude, latency, %PPI at four pre-pulse intensities, short-term habituation.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Short-term habituation analyzed across blocks within the session.

B4_ethological.evidence: Startle/PPI are reflex measures, not ethological behaviours.

B6_cognitive.evidence: PPI is a sensorimotor gating reflex, not learning.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Startle amplitude measured by force transducer, not behavioural classification from video.

E1_environment_type.evidence: StartFear Combined system, Panlab Harvard Apparatus.

E2_shelter.evidence: Startle holder is not a shelter.

D1_continuity.evidence: Basal startle was tested on one day, then PPI session 'on the day of the PPI and open field test'.

D2_session_duration.evidence: One test session... for a test session lasting 80 min in total.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Startle reflex tested on days before the open field and PPI tests, plus PPI day.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline within this assay.

D5_followup.evidence: Tests performed on the day following the last treatment (≥24 h post-dose).

assays.assay_description: Five rounds of two-bottle sucrose preference (~1 week apart): 2 baseline, 2 during the psilocybin microdosing regimen, and 1 final test 2 days after the last dose. Each test included an 8-h fast followed by 12-h overnight isolation in a home-cage-like cage with two pre-weighed bottles (1% sucrose vs water). Consumption was measured to calculate preference.

application_type.evidence: 0.05 mg/kg psilocybin s.c. every second day for 21 days

setup_habituation.evidence: Before the first test, all animals had a habituation session, during which all water bottles in primary housings were replaced for 24 h by water bottles with 1% sucrose.

setup_restrain.evidence: Animals were isolated for 12 h in a cage closely resembling their home cage, freely moving.

food_restriction.evidence: On day-1, animals were fasted (with free access to water) for an 8 h period in light (10-18).

water_restriction.evidence: Access to two water bottles containing premeasured 1% sucrose solution or regular water during the test.

time_to_assay.evidence: The first two tests were baseline recordings, the next two were made during the psilocybin microdosing regimen, and the final test was conducted on day two following the last saline/psilocybin treatment.

sample_size.evidence: The 16 animals were run in batches of 8 on separate days.

outcomes.summary: Control rats showed declining sucrose preference (to ~50%) during the repeated injection period, indicating stress-induced anhedonia. Psilocybin-treated rats maintained or increased preference (to ~92.7%) during treatment, returning to baseline after treatment ended.
outcomes.evidence: Control-injected animals indeed showed declining preference for sucrose during the treatment period to a mean of 50 ± 27%... psilocybin-treated animals did not show declining sucrose preference, but rather an increase to 92.7 ± 5.2% on their first within-treatment test.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Sucrose preference percentage (derived from consumption of two bottles) is a single preference measure.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Only total consumption per 12-h session reported; no within-session dynamics.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Isolated for 12 h in a cage closely resembling their home cage.

E2_shelter.evidence: No explicit shelter mentioned in the test cage.

E3_bedding.evidence: Bedding in test cage not explicitly described.

E4_nesting.evidence: Nesting in test cage not explicitly described.

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment items mentioned in test cage.

E6_spatial.evidence: Home-cage-like single compartment with two bottles.

E7_social_context.evidence: Each animal was isolated for 12 h.

E8_food_water.evidence: Access to two water bottles containing premeasured 1% sucrose solution or regular water during the 12-h test.

D1_continuity.evidence: 5 rounds of the sucrose preference test with approximately one week in between.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Each test consists of a 12-h isolated drinking period (consumption measured at start/end; behavioural recording window is the 12-h access period).

D4_baseline.evidence: The first two tests were baseline recordings.

D5_followup.evidence: The final test was conducted on day two following the last saline/psilocybin treatment.

assays.assay_description: 15-min test on an elevated plus maze (20x20 cm central platform, four 40-cm arms, two with 40-cm walls and two with 5-cm walls, raised 50 cm). Animals were naïve. Time/entries in open vs closed arms, locomotion, rearing and grooming were scored (Ethovision XT plus manual grooming/rearing scoring).

application_type.evidence: 0.05 mg/kg psilocybin s.c. every second day for 21 days

setup_habituation.evidence: Animals were naïve, being unhabituated to the open field and the elevated plus maze.

setup_restrain.evidence: An animal was placed into the central platform and recorded for 15 min, freely moving.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in the EPM during the 15-min test.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in the EPM during the 15-min test.

time_to_assay.evidence: behavioral tests were done on the day following the last treatment

sample_size.evidence: Rats in experiment 2 (Long Evans, n = 18, M, Janvier Labs).

outcomes.summary: Repeated low-dose psilocybin did not alter open- or closed-arm time or entries on the EPM, indicating no change in trait anxiety. Self-grooming frequency was reduced by ~48% in psilocybin-treated rats, without changes in locomotion or rearing.
outcomes.statistics: Self-grooming reduced by 48% (P value not explicitly reported); no significant difference in arm preference.
outcomes.evidence: We observed no change in preference for open or closed arms in the elevated plus maze... Interestingly, the frequency of self-grooming was reduced by 48% in the elevated plus maze, without changes in locomotion or rearing.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Distance, time in open arms, time in closed arms, arm entries, rearing, grooming.

B4_ethological.evidence: Rearing and grooming scored manually as distinct ethological acts.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Ethovision XT 11.5 (position tracking) plus manual scoring.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Plus-shaped platform raised 50 cm above the floor (standard EPM).

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM closed arms are part of apparatus design, not enclosed refuge (per rubric).

E6_spatial.evidence: Per rubric, EPM arms are open-ended extensions of a central platform, not distinct compartments.

D1_continuity.evidence: Each animal was recorded for 15 min on the EPM.

D3_recording_days.evidence: EPM performed on a single day per animal.

D4_baseline.evidence: Animals were naïve, no pre-drug EPM baseline.

D5_followup.evidence: EPM performed the day after the last s.c. injection (>24 h after last dose).

judge_notes: Merged candidate gptoss's separate Exp1 and Exp2 OFT into one Open Field Test assay (same paradigm/apparatus across cohorts; rubric collapses cohort/timepoint variants).
Kept Wet Back Shake (acute dose-response) as a separate assay from the chronic-regimen behaviours since it is a distinct acute pharmacological paradigm (still one HTR/WBS assay).

Set setup_restrain=yes for PPI based on rubric explicit example listing PPI startle chambers as body-restraint, even though the Panlab StartFear system can be used without tube restraint; medium confidence.

SPT D2 scored as 61 min-6 h (score 2) rather than >6 h: behavioural data is consumption integrated over 12 h, but the rubric scores single recording bouts and consumption windows are commonly binned; chose intermediate score and noted in evidence. D6 scored Yes since the access window spans >6 h overnight.
Dropped occupancy PET, in vitro receptor binding, functional cAMP/Ca2+ assays, and autoradiography as non-behavioural per rubric exclusions.
